'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Colombian conflict]]
**[[National Liberation Army (Colombia)|ELN]] rebels launch homemade [[Mortar (weapon)|mortar]] shells at a [[military base]] in [[El Carmen, Norte de Santander|El Carmen]], [[Norte de Santander]], [[Colombia]], killing nine [[Military Forces of Colombia|soldiers]] and injuring nine others. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/militants-kill-9-soldiers-attack-colombias-military-98205348 (ABC News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Sinking of [[MV Lady Mary Joy 3]]
**Thirty-one people are killed and more than 200 others are rescued after a ferry catches fire near an island in [[Basilan]], [[Philippines]]. At least seven are still missing. [https://apnews.com/article/philippines-ferry-fire-basilan-aca37f527e297842bde2ae5f837994a5 (AP)]
*Four people are killed by a storm in [[Syria]]. [https://apnews.com/article/syria-storm-wind-ports-36bd6a71a350c53dc85fd723dbef9dbf (AP)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2020–2023 H5N1 outbreak]]
**[[Chile]] detects its first case of [[Influenza A virus subtype H5N1|H5N1 bird flu]] in a 53-year-old man. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/chile-detects-first-case-bird-flu-human-2023-03-29/ (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Brazil–China relations]]
**[[Brazil]] and [[China]] sign an agreement to trade in their own currencies, ceasing the usage of the [[United States dollar]] as an intermediary. [https://www.straitstimes.com/world/china-brazil-strike-deal-to-ditch-dollar-for-trade (The Straits Times)]
*[[Burkina Faso–North Korea relations]]
**[[Burkina Faso]] formally resumes diplomatic relations with [[North Korea]] after suspending them in 2017 over the country's [[North Korea and weapons of mass destruction|nuclear weapons program]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/africa/burkina-faso-to-resume-diplomatic-relations-with-north-korea/2859013 (Anadolu Agency)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Myanmar]]'s ruling [[State Administration Council|military junta]] dissolves the [[National League for Democracy]], the [[List of political parties in Myanmar|political party]] of former [[State Counsellor of Myanmar|State Counsellor]]  [[Aung San Suu Kyi]]. [https://www3.nhk.or.jp/nhkworld/en/news/20230329_04/ (NHK)]
*[[Prime Minister of Fiji]] [[Sitiveni Rabuka]] announces that the [[Media Industry Development Authority of Fiji|Media Industry Development Authority]] will repeal a controversial 2010 law which strictly controlled media in the country. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/486965/fiji-to-scrap-media-law-for-growth-and-development-of-independent-journalism (RNZ)]
*[[Evan Gershkovich]], an American reporter at ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'', is arrested in [[Yekaterinburg]] by [[Russia]]'s [[Federal Security Service]] under charges of espionage. [https://www.rferl.org/a/wall-street-journal-gershkovich-russia-arrested-espionage/32341610.html (RFE/RL)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Repeal of the 2002 AUMF]]
**The [[U.S. Senate]] passes a bill to repeal the [[Authorization for Use of Military Force Against Iraq Resolution of 1991|1991]] and [[Authorization for Use of Military Force Against Iraq Resolution of 2002|2002]] Authorizations for Use of Military Force (AUMFs) that allowed the past [[wars in Iraq]], with a bipartisan majority of 66–30 votes. [https://www.reuters.com/world/us/majority-us-senate-backs-repeal-iraq-war-authorizations-voting-continues-2023-03-29 (Reuters)]
*[[President of Syria|Syrian President]] [[Bashar al-Assad]] reshuffles the [[government of Syria|government]]'s cabinet amid [[inflation|an increase in prices]] and shortages of food due to the severe [[economy of Syria|economic situation the country]], which was worsened by [[2023 Turkey–Syria earthquake|the recent earthquake]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2023/03/29/syria-government-assad-reshuffle-economic-crisis/86d7f3c2-ce0a-11ed-8907-156f0390d081_story.html (AP via ''The Washington Post'')]
*[[President of the United Arab Emirates|UAE President]] [[Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan]] announces that he has named his son [[Khaled bin Mohamed Al Nahyan]] as the [[Abu Dhabi]] [[Al Nahyan|Crown Prince]]. [[City Football Group]] owner [[Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan]] is also appointed as [[Vice President of the United Arab Emirates|Vice President]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/amp/news/2023/3/29/uae-leader-designates-his-son-khaled-as-crown-prince (Al Jazeera)]
 
'''Science and technology'''
*The [[World Meteorological Organization]] announces that [[Hurricane Fiona|Fiona]] and [[Hurricane Ian|Ian]] will be retired from future use during [[Atlantic hurricane season|Atlantic hurricane seasons]] following the destruction caused [[2022 Atlantic hurricane season|last year]], and will be replaced by Farrah and Idris in 2028. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/fiona-ian-retired-hurricane-names-world-meteorological-organization/ (CBS News)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2023 FIFA U-20 World Cup]]
**[[FIFA]] strips [[Indonesia]] of hosting this year's [[FIFA U-20 World Cup]] tournament after the [[List of governors of Bali|Governor of Bali]] [[I Wayan Koster]] refused to host the [[Israel national under-19 football team]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/football/2023/mar/29/fifa-strips-indonesia-of-the-right-to-host-footballs-under-20-world-cup (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2022–23 NBA season]]
**In [[basketball]], the [[Sacramento Kings]] make the [[2023 NBA playoffs|NBA playoffs]] for the first time since [[2005–06 Sacramento Kings season|2006]], ending their [[List of NBA franchise post-season droughts#Longest post-season droughts in team history|17-year]] playoff drought, the longest in NBA history. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/kings/2023/03/29/sacramento-kings-end-longest-playoff-drought-nba-history/11558656002/ (''USA Today'')] [https://fox40.com/sports/basketball/kings/playoff-bound-sacramento-kings-clinch-long-awaited-postseason-berth/amp/ (KTXL-TV)]
